Adam Blevins began working in the entertainment industry in 2022 as a Staff Writer for Agents of Fandom, where he progressed to Senior Editor and interviewed talent from Marvel Studios, House of the Dragon, and Planet of the Apes. He joined Collider as a News Author in April 2024, was promoted to a Senior position in December 2024, and has written over 3,000 articles for the site, including exclusives relating to Avengers: Doomsday, The Penguin, Star Wars: Skeleton Crew, and more. He primarily writes about the latest box office numbers and the hottest movies and TV shows on streaming, while also covering superhero and sci-fi news. He has completed a set visit for The Chosen and even has several months of experience writing Gaming Features at ScreenRant. You can find him on X, LinkedIn, and Muckrack.

What a year it’s been for Rebecca Ferguson, and to top it all off, one of the most underrated projects of her career is finding a second wind on streaming. To kick off 2026, Ferguson starred opposite Chris Pratt in the Amazon MGM sci-fi thriller, Mercy, which bombed at the box office before going on to become one of the biggest movies of the year on Prime Video. Ferguson also headlined one of the biggest sci-fi shows of the summer in Silo on Apple TV, and she’s returning to her role as Juliette in the fourth and final season of the show next summer. Ferguson will also reprise her role as Lady Jessica later this year in Dune: Part Three, but she has confirmed that she will only have one scene in the franchise-capping sci-fi threequel.

Rebecca Ferguson has starred in enough movies to this point in her career that it’s only natural for some to have been largely forgotten to the scope of time. One of said projects that fans don’t often remember is Doctor Sleep, the legacy sequel to The Shining starring Ferguson as the featured villain, Rose the Hat. Ewan McGregor, best known for playing Obi-Wan Kenobi in Star Wars, also has a key role in Doctor Sleep, along with Cliff Curtis and Zahn McClarnon. Based on the novel by Stephen King, Doctor Sleep was written and directed by Mike Flanagan, who is a frequent adapter of King’s work. Seven years after Doctor Sleep hit theaters, the film is still not available to watch on streaming, but fans are checking it out in droves on VOD platforms like Prime Video and Apple TV.
